source.title: The Predictive Normalized Maximum Likelihood for Over-parameterized Linear Regression with Norm Constraint: Regret and Double Descent

page_placements.theme: Information criteria, regret and marginal likelihood need not agree with risk

record.tranche_reason: Tests double descent in over-parameterized linear regression on UCI datasets, using test logloss while varying the parameter-to-training-size ratio. This is a conceptual test in a different model family and setting from the deep-network claim.
record.gate_note: The paper varies training-set size on UCI datasets and reports test-logloss curves. It also reports pNML regret curves, which are related to but are not themselves test error; those are recorded under fits_no_version. The cited findings in Related Work are not rows. Figure 3 varies a regret threshold, not model size, epochs, or sample size.
record.test_reason: On nine UCI datasets, M is fixed and training-set size N is varied for the minimum-norm linear-regression learner and the pNML learner. Test logloss rises as N falls toward M=N, then falls again as N shrinks further (Fig. 2 top). This is a sample-wise double-descent result, in a new setting, on the more-data-can-hurt claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors' main contribution is an analytical upper bound on pNML regret for over-parameterized linear regression, whose prediction equals the MN solution. Double descent is a demonstration: test logloss for MN and pNML peaks at M=N when training-set size is varied on nine UCI sets, and empirical regret and its bound show the same shape.
record.recipe_differences: Uses over-parameterized linear regression on UCI datasets, varies training-set size relative to feature count, and measures test logloss; it does not reproduce the original deep-network experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and M/N ratio vary. The authors optimize σ² on a validation set for both learners.

fits_no_version.finding: Empirical pNML regret and its analytical upper bound peak at M=N and fall as M/N increases, tracking test logloss on the UCI sets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A pointwise pNML regret, or its upper bound, tracks the sample-wise double-descent curve of test logloss in minimum-norm linear regression.

fits_no_version.finding: In synthetic trigonometric interpolation with 8 points, the M=10 model has larger regret and a far larger MN norm (295,552) than M=20 (0.15) or M=50 (0.04).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Past the interpolation point, more parameters can lower both MN-solution norm and pNML regret.

record.problems: The plotted curves provide no numerical point values in the text. The reported UCI results use 5 or 20 train-test splits, and the experiments are limited to linear regression. The plotted 95% confidence intervals are described as calculated across different train-test splits.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results omitted. Figure 3 evaluates performance after filtering samples by regret threshold, rather than testing model size, epochs, or training-set size. Related-work claims are cited findings, not this study's results.

untested.parts: No deep networks and no model-size sweep.
Only the linear minimum-norm and pNML learners are tested, without label-noise or regularization variation. Deep networks are not tested.
Capacity (M) is never varied. Only the parameter-to-sample ratio is varied, by changing N.
No effective-complexity measure is tested as predicting the peak location.
No noise or regularization manipulation. σ² is tuned on a validation set, but its effect on the peak is not reported.

record.verdict_notes: All curve evidence is figure only, with no numeric values in the text. σ² is optimized on a validation set, and logloss depends on it. The reader's V4 link is removed because the M/N axis is moved only by changing N. Figure 3 is a regret-threshold filtering analysis and is correctly left out.

versions.untested_parts: Deep networks; no deep-network model-size sweep is reported.
Tested by varying training-set size in the reported UCI linear-regression experiments, not across deep networks or other model families.
Tested for over-parameterized linear regression on UCI datasets; not across other model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as predicting peak location across size, epochs, and sample size.

No test of whether noise drives the peak, whether multiple peaks arise, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes the peak. The paper optimizes σ² on a validation set but does not test these claims.
No test of whether an effective-parameter count turns the second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

labels.reason: Section 6.2 and Figure 2 describe both learners' logloss declining as N decreases beyond M=N; reversing this comparison gives harmful sample increases toward interpolation from N<M (r01–r18).

relation.reason: Section 6.2 varies training-set size and measures test logloss; its own results directly bear on whether increasing sample size near interpolation can hurt.

tranche.reason: The study reports its own sample-wise double-descent results for minimum-norm and pNML linear regression on nine UCI datasets, providing a new setting with results on V3.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is arXiv:2102.07181v2, titled Distribution Free Uncertainty for the Minimum Norm Solution of Over-parameterized Linear Regression; the pack uses a different title. UCI results use validation-tuned variance and plotted logloss with 95% confidence intervals; they do not provide numerical pairwise effect estimates.
